flags.purpose: Dumps the complete Windows Firewall with Advanced Security configuration into a script file for backup and documentation.
flags.security_use_case: Backup firewall configuration before changes and preserve evidence during incident response.
flags.risk_if_misused: Backup file contains detailed security policy; must be stored securely.
flags.safe_followup: Use 'netsh advfirewall restore' to restore; archive backup securely.

flags.purpose: Displays firewall state (ON/OFF) for Domain, Private, and Public profiles.
flags.security_use_case: Quick verification that firewall protection is enabled across all network profiles.
flags.threat_detected: Firewall disabled on any profile increasing attack surface.
flags.safe_followup: Enable firewall if any profile is OFF.

flags.example_command: netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on
flags.purpose: Enables Windows Firewall on all profiles to block unsolicited inbound connections.
flags.security_use_case: Immediate defensive action if firewall was disabled by attacker or misconfiguration.
flags.risk_if_misused: May disrupt applications that depend on open ports; requires rule tuning.
flags.safe_followup: Create necessary allow rules for legitimate apps; monitor connectivity.

flags.example_command: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="BlockInbound445" dir=in action=block protocol=TCP localport=445
flags.purpose: Creates a new firewall rule to allow or block specific traffic patterns.
flags.security_use_case: Block sensitive ports (e.g., SMB 445) to prevent lateral movement and exploits.
flags.threat_detected: Unauthorized inbound access to sensitive services.
flags.risk_if_misused: Incorrect rule may block critical services or business apps.
flags.safe_followup: Document rule; test impact; delete if misconfigured.

flags.example_command: netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name="OldBlockRule"
flags.purpose: Deletes a firewall rule by name to remove obsolete or incorrect entries.
flags.security_use_case: Clean up unnecessary rules or fix misconfigurations causing issues.
flags.risk_if_misused: May remove legitimate security control if not reviewed.
flags.safe_followup: Backup rules before deletion; re-audit firewall after change.

flags.purpose: Exports current firewall policy into a .wfw file for reuse or deployment.
flags.security_use_case: Distribute hardened firewall configuration across systems.
flags.risk_if_misused: Sensitive policy file; must be handled securely.

flags.purpose: Imports firewall policy from a .wfw file, replacing current configuration.
flags.risk_if_misused: Overwrites existing rules; may break connectivity.
flags.safe_followup: Backup current config before import; test on non-production system.

flags.example_command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all dir=in
flags.purpose: Lists all inbound firewall rules with their state and action.
flags.security_use_case: Audit inbound allow rules that may expose services to attackers.
flags.threat_detected: Overly permissive inbound rules on Public profile.

powerful_combinations.command: netsh advfirewall show allprofiles & netsh advfirewall show global
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Displays firewall state and global logging settings for a complete posture overview.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Initial audit during incident response to verify defenses and logging.

powerful_combinations.command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all dir=in | findstr /i "Enable Yes"
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Quickly lists all enabled inbound rules that allow traffic into the system.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Finding unintended exposed services or ports.

powerful_combinations.command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all dir=out
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Shows outbound rules to understand egress filtering configuration.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Determining if malware command-and-control traffic could exit the network.
